tools.name: list_allowed_directories
tools.description: List directories this MCP server can access.

tools.name: set_allowed_directory
tools.description:
Set a single active allowed directory at runtime.

Intended for user-selected workspace roots from frontend/orchestrator.

tools.name: set_allowed_directories
tools.description: Set multiple active allowed directories at runtime.

tools.name: reset_allowed_directories
tools.description: Reset allowed directories back to initial startup configuration.

tools.name: list_directory
tools.description: List immediate directory contents.

tools.name: directory_tree
tools.description: Return a recursive JSON tree of directories/files.

tools.name: read_text_file
tools.description:
Read UTF-8 text content from a file.
REQUIRED: 'target_file_path' is the path to the file.

Optional slicing:
- head: first N lines
- tail: last N lines

Optional hash-anchoring:
- hashline: if True, return content annotated with line-hash anchors
  (format: 'LINENUM#HASH|TEXT') suitable for use with edit_file_hashline.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description:
Backward-compatible alias for line-ranged file reads.

This keeps compatibility with clients that call `read_file` while
internally reusing the `read_text_file` implementation.

tools.name: read_multiple_files
tools.description: Read multiple text files; failures are captured per file.

tools.name: get_file_info
tools.description: Get metadata for a file or directory.

tools.name: create_directory
tools.description: Create directory recursively; succeeds if it already exists.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description:
Write text to file (UTF-8).
REQUIRED: 'target_file_path' is the path to the file.
REQUIRED: 'content' is the text to write.

Safety:
- Refuses writes larger than MCP_MAX_WRITE_BYTES
- Atomic replace through temp file

tools.name: append_file
tools.description: Append UTF-8 text to an existing or new file.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description:
Replace text in a file.

REQUIRED: 'target_file_path' is the path to the file.
REQUIRED: 'exact_text_to_replace' is the EXACT block of text to find and replace.
          NOTE: use 'exact_text_to_replace', NOT 'old_text' or 'old_content'.
REQUIRED: 'new_text_content' is the replacement text.
          NOTE: use 'new_text_content', NOT 'new_text'.

tools.name: move_file
tools.description: Move or rename file/directory within allowed directories.

tools.name: delete_path
tools.description:
Delete a file or directory.
Safety:
- directories require recursive=true

tools.name: search_files
tools.description:
Recursively search by glob-style filename pattern.

Example patterns:
- *.py
- *config*

tools.name: search_web
tools.description:
Search the web for real-time information, news, current events, or general knowledge.

Use this tool when you need information that is not available in your local workspace or training data,
especially for topics that change frequently like weather, news, or recent developments in technology.

tools.name: fetch_url
tools.description: Fetch a webpage and extract readable text content.

tools.name: server_status
tools.description: Operational status and safety config summary for auditing/debugging.

tools.name: read_media_file_base64
tools.description:
Read binary file and return base64-encoded content.

This is useful for images/audio similar to common filesystem MCP servers.

tools.name: write_json_file
tools.description: Write JSON object to a file using safe atomic write.

tools.name: edit_diff
tools.description:
Apply a unified diff (patch) to a file.
REQUIRED: 'target_file_path' must be the path to the file you want to edit.
REQUIRED: 'diff' must be a valid unified diff string starting with '---' and '+++'.

If this fails, the tool will return the current content of the file to help you fix the hunk context.

tools.name: edit_file_hashline
tools.description:
Edit a file using hash-anchored DSL. Atomic: ALL hashes are validated
before any bytes are written. If any hash mismatches the actual file
content, the entire operation is rejected with an error — the file is
left completely unchanged.

Use read_text_file with hashline=True to get anchor values for a file,
then construct the edit DSL from those anchors.

edits DSL format (blocks separated by ---):

  = START#HASH..END#HASH    replace the line range with the following lines
  + ANCHOR#HASH             insert the following lines after the anchor line
  < ANCHOR#HASH             insert the following lines before the anchor line
  - START#HASH..END#HASH    delete the line range (no following content)

Example:
  = 3#a1b2..5#c3d4
  new line replacing lines 3-5
  ---
  + 7#d4e5
  line inserted after line 7
  ---
  - 10#f6g7..12#h8i9

tools.name: create_project
tools.description:
Create a new project structure at the specified path.
Supported templates: python-basic, node-basic, fastapi-jwt.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description:
Replace the current todo list with a new set of tasks.

Each task dict must have at minimum a 'content' key (str).
Optional keys: 'status' ('pending'|'in_progress'|'completed'), 'priority' ('high'|'medium'|'low').

Use this to track multi-step work plans so the user can see progress.

tools.name: todo_read
tools.description: Return the current todo list.

tools.name: bash_exec
tools.description:
Execute a shell command and return its output.

- Output is capped at 10 000 lines (PTY scrollback limit); excess lines are
  replaced with a truncation notice.
- Timeout default is 30 s; max is 120 s.
- A small set of obviously destructive commands is unconditionally blocked.
- The working directory defaults to the first allowed directory (or repo root).
- Uses a PTY on Linux/macOS for realistic terminal output; falls back to
  subprocess.PIPE on systems where PTY is unavailable.

Use for: running tests, git commands, build scripts, inspecting processes.
Do NOT use for: interactive programs, long-running daemons (use & to background).

tools.name: grep_codebase
tools.description:
Search for a regex pattern across files in the codebase.

Uses ripgrep (rg) when available, falls back to Python's re module.

path.description: Directory or file to search in (defaults to allowed root).

file_glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files, e.g. '*.py', '*.ts'.

max_results.description: Maximum number of matches to return (cap 500).

tools.name: search_symbols
tools.description:
Search for code symbols (functions, classes, methods) by name pattern.
Supports glob patterns (e.g. 'get_*', '*Handler'). Uses tree-sitter when
available, falls back to regex grep.

query.description: Symbol name pattern (supports * and ? glob wildcards)

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

kinds.description: Symbol types to find ('function','class','method','variable'). Default: all

tools.name: get_repo_map
tools.description:
Get a high-level overview of the project structure.

Returns a text summary including: top-level directories, file counts by
language, and the first docstring/comment line of key entry-point files
(main.py, app.py, index.ts, etc.).

max_depth.description: How many directory levels to traverse (1–6).

tools.name: propose_plan
tools.description:
Propose a multi-step plan for a complex task.

Call this before starting a large task so the user can review the approach.
The plan is saved to the todo list so it persists across turns.

goal.description: High-level description of what you're trying to accomplish.

steps.description: Ordered list of concrete actions you plan to take.

tools.name: view_git_diff
tools.description: Show git diff for a file or directory (read-only, no side effects).

path.description: File or directory to diff, relative to project root. Defaults to '.'.

staged.description: If True, show staged changes (git diff --cached). Defaults to False.

base.description: Base ref to diff against, e.g. 'HEAD', 'main', 'HEAD~1'. Defaults to 'HEAD'.

tools.name: watch_file
tools.description: Start watching a file or directory for changes. Changes are logged to the event history.

watch_id.description: Unique identifier for this watcher (used to stop it later)

path.description: File or directory path to watch

pattern.description: Optional glob pattern to filter files (e.g. '*.py'). Only for directories.

tools.name: stop_watch_file
tools.description: Stop a file watcher started with watch_file.

tools.name: invoke_skill
tools.description:
Invoke a named skill to load its full instructions.
Skills are defined in SKILL.md files under ~/.atri/skills/ or .atri/skills/.

tools.name: read_tool_result
tools.description:
Read the full content of a distilled tool result that was truncated.
The turn_id is shown in the truncation notice (e.g. '3_read_text_file').

tools.name: retain
tools.description: Store a persistent key-value memory that survives session compaction and restarts.

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Retrieve a previously retained memory by key. Returns the stored value or a not-found message.

tools.name: list_memories
tools.description: List all retained memory keys.
